newsitem.title: USA: Postal supervisor gunned down in Nevada - police.
newsitem.headline: Postal supervisor gunned down in Nevada - police.

text.p: Police in Nevada said a postal supervisor was gunned down on Thursday by a disgruntled ex-postal employee who surrendered and confessed to authorities shortly after the shooting.

James Brown, 59, a supervisor in the labour relations department at the main post office for Las Vegas, was shot in the head in the employee parking lot as he arrived for work early on Thursday. He was pronounced dead at the scene, Police Lt. Wayne Petersen said.
Charles Jennings, who had been fired earlier this year from his job at the post office, surrendered to a police officer about 30 minutes after the incident, authorities said.
Jennings told the officer that he had just shot someone, according to Sgt. Greg McCurdy, a spokesman for the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.
Police said Brown had represented the post office during hearings to review Jennings' dismissal. Jennings was notified earlier this week that an arbitrator upheld his termination.

Jennings, 41, was taken into custody and was charged with murder with a deadly weapon. A handgun was recovered from his vehicle, which police believe to be the murder weapon, Petersen said. He was being held in a county jail facility.
